text:
Samir: quick heads-up — I'm swapping out of the evening shift at 22:00 PT. Current plan: Primary = Olivia, Secondary = Lee. There's a 45m gap starting ~22:15 where neither is fully desktop-available. Need a warm volunteer for 22:15-23:00. :wave:

Olivia: I can take primary until 22:15 PT, after that I've got a calendar block. I can triage pager summaries from phone but won't be able to stay on the bridge.

Lee: I can cover 22:15-23:00 but I'm remote on unstable cell. If we get repeated pages, please escalate to Priya after 10m no-ack.

Priya: I can be on-call-standby for that 22:15-23:00 window. If it's a Sev1 (customer-impacting outage) page me immediately and also ping @oncall-bot escalate. For lower-sev noise, let Lee handle first. :thumbsup:

Samir: agreed. I'm creating a short handoff note in the runbook and will attach relevant dashboard links. Key runbook pointers: error-rate threshold (5% sustained over 5m) = Sev1, token-generation latency >2s p95 for 3m = Sev2. If unsure, escalate.

oncall-bot: Automated message — IncidentTriageBot detected an abnormal error spike on /generate endpoint at 21:47 PT (score 5). Suggested severity: P1 if sustained. Action: /incident bridge create to start call. Auto-escalation timers initialized: 10m -> secondary, 20m -> sre-lead, 30m -> eng-director.

Samir: starting manual triage: checked logs, spike seems correlated with a canary rollout. If it continues, rollback canary tag 2026-03-14b. Whoever is primary — be ready to run rollback steps (see Runbook > Deploy rollback snippet).

Olivia: I'm attaching the quick rollback commands here in case I get paged and can't join the bridge: 
```
# quick rollback
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/gateway gateway=image:2026-03-14a
kubectl rollout status deploy/gateway -n inference
```

Lee: good. If primary doesn't ack within 10m, page secondary (Lee). If Lee doesn't ack in 10m after that, page Priya (sre fallback). If Priya doesn't respond in additional 10m, escalate to SRE Lead and open an exec channel.

Priya: clarification — page sequence we should use in PagerDuty: Primary -> SMS+Mobile push to Secondary -> Slack mention to @Priya (if SMS fails) -> page SRE Lead (on-call list). For Sev1 also create bridge immediately and DM the on-call execs list.

Samir: note for handoff log: update the shift doc with primary/secondary names and exact coverage windows. I'll add a line: "22:15-23:00 warm standby: Priya (accept pages)".

Olivia: also small change to paging rules: for auth failures (auth errors >3% 2m) treat as Sev2, do not escalate to execs unless customer-visible token failures >10% 5m.

oncall-bot: Reminder: use `/incident note add <id> "handoff summary"` to attach handoff notes. Auto closes triage if no further spikes in 15m.

Lee: if you're paging someone and they don't respond, always include the short context in the first page: 1) service 2) impact 3) last action. Makes it way faster to decide whether to escalate.

Priya: agreed. Example page body we use: "generate-service: 5% error, p95 latency 2.8s, rollback available (tag 2026-03-14a). Need ack + bridge?"

Samir: final checklist before I sign off: 1) Update shift doc (done) 2) Confirm warm-standby (Priya confirmed) 3) Drop rollback snippet in thread (done) 4) If Sev1 -> create bridge + add execs + mark customer-impact true.

Olivia: noted. I'll be primary until 22:15 and will start bridge if incident persists. If I get paged and can't join, I'll DM Lee to takeover.

Lee: I'll monitor for pages at 22:15-23:00. Priya on standby to escalate to if I don't respond within 10m. Thanks.

Priya: tldr — coverage gap covered, paging ladder confirmed, runbook + rollback in thread. Ping me if anyone needs me earlier. :rotating_light:
